verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I want to remind you of the good news I preached to you. You received it, and you stand firm in it.
By this good news you are saved, if you hold on to the message I preached to you. Otherwise you have believed for nothing.
What I received, I passed on to you as most important: Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures said.
He was buried, and he was raised to life on the third day, as the Scriptures said.
He appeared to Cephas, and then to the twelve apostles.
After that, he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at the same time. Most of them are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
Last of all he appeared to me too, as to someone born at the wrong time.
For I am the least of the apostles. I do not even deserve to be called an apostle, because I attacked God's church.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace to me was not wasted. I worked harder than all of them. Yet it was not really me, but God's grace that was with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
If we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, how can some of you say that the dead are not raised to life?
If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
More than that, we would be lying about God. We have said that God raised Christ from the dead. But he did not raise him if the dead are not raised.
For if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is worthless, and you are still in your sins.
Then those who have died believing in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is only for this life, we should be pitied more than anyone else.
But Christ really has been raised from the dead. He is the first of the great harvest of all who have died.
Death came through a man, and rising from the dead also comes through a man.
For as everyone dies because of Adam, so everyone who belongs to Christ will be made alive.
But each in the right order: Christ first, and then, when he comes, those who belong to him.
Then the end will come. Christ will destroy every ruler, every authority and every power, and hand over the kingdom to God the Father.
For Christ must rule until God has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For the Scriptures say, "God has put everything under his feet." But when it says everything has been put under him, it clearly does not include God himself, who put everything under Christ.
When all this is done, the Son himself will be made subject to God, who put everything under him. Then God will be everything to everyone.
If there is no rising from the dead, what will people do who are baptised for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptised for them?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
Brothers and sisters, I face death every day. That is as sure as my pride in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus only for human reasons, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, then "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
Do not be fooled: "Bad company ruins good character."
Come back to your senses as you should, and stop sinning. Some of you do not know God. I say this to shame you.
But someone may ask, "How are the dead raised? What kind of body will they have?"
How foolish! What you plant does not come to life unless it dies first.
When you plant, you do not plant the whole plant that will grow. You plant only a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
But God gives it the body he has chosen, and to each kind of seed he gives its own body.
Not all flesh is the same. People have one kind of flesh, animals another, birds another and fish another.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. The glory of the heavenly bodies is one kind, and the glory of the earthly bodies is another.
The sun has one kind of glory, the moon another and the stars another. And each star is different from the others in its glory.
It will be the same when the dead are raised. The body that is buried will decay, but the body that is raised will never decay.
It is buried in shame, but raised in glory. It is buried in weakness, but raised in power.
It is buried as a natural body, but raised as a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
The Scriptures say, "The first man, Adam, became a living person." But the last Adam, Christ, became a spirit who gives life.
The spiritual did not come first. The natural came first, and then the spiritual.
The first man was made from the dust of the earth. The second man came from heaven.
Those who belong to the earth are like the man made of dust. And those who belong to heaven are like the man from heaven.
Just as we have been like the man made of dust, we will also be like the man from heaven.
Brothers and sisters, I tell you this: flesh and blood cannot receive God's kingdom. What decays cannot receive what never decays.
Listen, I tell you a secret. We will not all die, but we will all be changed.
It will happen in a moment, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised never to decay, and we will be changed.
For our bodies that decay must be clothed with what never decays. Our bodies that die must be clothed with what never dies.
When this happens, the Scriptures will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
"Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?"
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the Lord's work, because you know that your work in the Lord is never wasted.
